sections.value:
PR #240 - round 2, final C34 round
Result: pass-with-notes
Head: 520e5d196305eb61a668bba93257719f0095272f
Delta basis: 69c0516d8879793b1776753e6d75839931608ce0
Answers: 01a1ecb9-e9a3-7f21-ab9c-634d50fb6f47

No remaining blocking normal-use correctness finding in this delta. S240-001
is fixed, including the supported Linux in-place-upgrade case discovered
while reviewing the intermediate head. No verdict was published at that
superseded head. No local build or test ran.

Identity and the false-negative question

- runs_under now starts above the statusline process and stops at the first
  recognized harness host. It checks that host's PID AND observed local
  process start against the seat. It never keeps climbing after encountering
  a different recognized host. Thus A -> B -> sh -> statusline cannot use A's
  seat, while B's seat is accepted with or without the shell.
- The new regression pins both pane and paneless rejection of A, acceptance
  of B directly and through sh, and A's own direct statusline acceptance.
- The native extension's resolveNativeHost records the actual Copilot host
  ancestor, not the extension child or pane shell. Registration independently
  verifies the executable and incarnation; a Node npm launcher is explicitly
  not the native host. The daemon also recognizes an actual node process
  running the Copilot index.js entrypoint; node is in the display boundary's
  host set.
- Launch evidence is empirical, not inferred from documentation. I read all
  116 rows of the author's f198-statusline-ppid-raw.txt. The author captured
  $$, $PPID and pane immediately before the managed script's exec, then
  restored the script. Examples include child 66873 -> parent 2529 on %135,
  66197 -> 19124 on %159, 66464 -> 87819 on %145, and 66605 -> 11136 on %118.
  The author correlates those parents to the corresponding registered host
  PIDs and reports their p_comm as copilot. The reported topology is:
  node npm-loader -> outer copilot -> inner copilot (recorded seat) -> statusline.
  Independently, this review seat's recorded PID 49233 is a native copilot
  executable with ucomm copilot, not the npm loader.
- The installed npm loader spawns the platform-native binary before its JS
  fallback. It is ABOVE the host in this observed native topology, not a Node
  helper between host and statusline. No observed normal managed invocation
  here inserts such a helper. An arbitrary custom Node wrapper would indeed
  be a boundary and could hide the seat; do not claim this heuristic supports
  every possible custom command or future Copilot topology.
- The build's statusLine documentation specifies command/stdin/refresh
  behavior but does not document the spawning parent topology. It is not
  evidence of direct spawning; the live capture above is that evidence.

Linux upgrade and macOS inspection

- The final production reader calls linux_exe_name on the /proc/PID/exe
  target. It strips one exact trailing " (deleted)" marker before extracting
  the basename, matching registration's established normalization. An
  upgraded copilot therefore remains the nearest recognized host: it neither
  disappears from its own display nor permits climbing to an outer seat.
- This fixes the concrete intermediate-head regression, not speculative
  hardening: in-place upgrades are an existing supported path documented in
  docs/how/copilot-native-extension.md, and registration already has a
  replaced-executable witness. The new helper regression passes in final CI.
- macOS parent_and_host_name delegates to the existing ProcBSDShortInfo
  reader, which checks pbsi_pid and returns pbsi_ppid plus p_comm. All eight
  recognized names fit in its 15-byte name payload, including copilot/node.
  The matching start read and local timebase are unchanged. No new shell,
  PATH lookup, process launch or unsafe block is introduced.
- macOS cfg was read by eye, NOT independently compiled or tested here.
  Linux CI is not evidence that the macOS cfg compiled.

F195 regression additions

The HTTP lease regression now reads state and list after renewal and asserts
the new display fields are absent. The boot-grace regression asserts the
exact never-renewed line alongside active process liveness. These close the
relevant round-one display-transition notes. Production lease logic and the
renewal loop are unchanged in the reviewed delta.

Cost - delta only

- ZERO new launches and ZERO additional daemon requests per render. The
  lookup remains in-process: macOS short BSD info; Linux stat plus read_link.
  The final deleted-marker correction is pure string/path processing.
- Compared with round 1, the common direct case reads self and its parent
  (two process records), then the matching host's start. macOS preserves the
  name the old parent reader already obtained; it also needs the parent's
  record to classify that host. Linux adds executable read_link per inspected
  process. At the configured 10-second refresh, this scales with rendering
  Copilot sessions, plus their event-driven refreshes, never a new poll loop.
- The hard bound is one initial self read plus up to 64 ancestor records:
  at most 65 process records per render, not 64 total. No read launches ps,
  tmux or another command. The new code has no new spawn-counter site.
- State/list production and their per-call costs are unchanged in this
  delta. The earlier baseline remains the pre-deploy receipt, not an
  after-deploy measurement.

C34 follow-up R240-F1 (documentation precision only, NOT a merge gate):
the walk's "at most 64 processes" wording should say 64 ancestors plus self.
Likewise, an unrecognized name is not generically guaranteed to accept fewer
seats: it can allow a walk to an outer host. The concrete supported Linux
replacement case is fixed. No further round or extra machinery is requested.

Verification

- just pr-freeze 240 --worktree: FINAL at the full head above, ls-remote/gh
  agreement, main base, CLEAN, five latest checks pass, not draft, no
  migrations, clean detached review-240-520e5d1 checkout.
- git diff --check <basis>..<head>: exit 0.
- Successful exact-head CI run 44231858379: rust-lint, rust-test, check (22)
  and check (24) all succeeded. The latest delivers run 44231869562 passed;
  its older cancelled attempt is not the final result.
- Successful rust-test job 134558560135 uploaded JUnit artifact 14395228809.
  Its 2474 test cases have zero failures/errors; nextest reports 2474 passed,
  6 skipped. I selected the artifact from that successful job's upload log.
- Explicit final-artifact PASS: nested-Copilot boundary regression, foreign
  seat regression, real process-name reader, Linux deleted-suffix helper,
  F195 lapse/recovery HTTP test, F195 never-renewed HTTP test, registration's
  replaced-executable witness, and every_daemon_launch_site_records_itself.
- No local Cargo, TS test, dependency installation or symlink was used.
  No product source edits were made by the reviewer.

Owed after merge/reinstall/bounce, not before merging

Repeat the two live cost instruments over a known interval, with daemon CPU
and RSS, and keep the after-deploy receipt. The round-one reviewer output
e3629dd3 contains the before-deploy counters and whole-machine sample.
Smoke registered-own identity and second-server/unregistered identity, and
confirm lapsed native receiver state/list visibility and clearing on renewal.

Harness feedback

magicWand: reuse the existing executable-replacement witness at the display
boundary so registration and display cannot silently disagree again.
difficulties: Linux CI was green while replacement normalization was covered
only in registration. The final new helper regression encodes the discovered
cross-path failure. Observation captured as pij-mere-lizard/DL-001.
